name: slack
description: Use Slack through the venue's bindings: post plain text to allowed channels and threads, understand Slack-originated conversations, and check binding status. Load for Slack communication; it reveals separate binding-management guidance for creating, repairing or deleting bindings.

content.inline:
## Slack
A binding connects one Slack app installation to an agent or operation and answers DMs and channel mentions by itself: a reply in the current conversation needs no tool. Use these for anything else.

- `send {bot?, channel, text, thread_ts?}` posts as the binding's bot. `channel` is a channel ID the binding allows (C… or G… for channels, D… for a DM); `thread_ts` keeps the post in that thread. Omit `bot` only when you own exactly one binding.
- `bots {}` lists the bindings you may use with their state, webhook path or Socket Mode `connection`, and receipt counts; tokens are never returned.

Inbound messages arrive as `{text, via}`: `via.from` is the sender's Slack user ID, `via.chat` the channel ID, `via.thread` the thread timestamp, `via.message_id` the message's own timestamp, `via.team` the workspace and `via.access` either `allow` or `open`. The venue supplies `via`; it names a Slack account, not a Covia principal, and grants no venue authority. Slack gives IDs, not names, so keep who-is-who in memory.

Rules:
- Text goes out exactly as written, up to 4000 characters: Markdown, `<@U…>` mentions and `<url|text>` links appear literally, so write plain text and bare URLs.
- Never guess a channel or user ID; use one from `via`, the user, or `bots`. A refusal saying the destination is not allowed is the binding's `allowChannels` at work, not a fault.
- A channel post is visible to everyone in it; confirm the channel and content before posting unless the task explicitly authorises it.
- Keep timestamps as strings. A failed send may still have been delivered; do not retry it automatically.
- Reading Slack (history, user names, search) is a different skill: the `slack` connection under connections, which calls the Slack Web API with your own `s/SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` and needs the matching app scopes.
